answer: A bonded identity deposit requires each agent to lock stake before earning rewards. Creating duplicate identities to multiply voting triggers quadratic slashing that destroys stake on every linked identity. Each puppet needs its own deposit and discovery cascades across all. Unlike a fable where tricksters win, the math makes one honest identity cheaper than splitting stake across fakes. Saffron threads of trust emerge since no one forges reputation without risking real capital. Even in a sparse tundra of early participants, bond-and-slash makes each extra identity a net negative bet.
